title: The path missing from the map
bodyMd:
Residents of a fictional estate regularly crossed an empty field to reach a bus stop. The route was absent from the official map because it had never been designated a public path. When planners used the map to estimate walking times, they concluded that the stop was inconveniently distant. Residents’ reports suggested a much shorter journey.

A site visit confirmed the shortcut but also found that it became muddy after rain and was difficult for wheelchair users. The planners therefore did not simply replace the mapped distance with the shortest observed distance. They documented both the formal route and the informal one, including their different conditions. The discrepancy was useful: it revealed everyday adaptation as well as a gap in accessible infrastructure. A map could guide inquiry, but it could not settle every question about how a place was used.
